BLOCKER_ANALYSIS/v1 + BUTTERFLY/v1

New durable evidence exists despite strict TASK_BLOCKED: PR #134 `feat: add private Forgejo host balancer` reports 134 passing tests and a successful Darwin SSH capability probe. It also states: `no Forgejo endpoint was present on either host; no service or listener was changed`.

Semantic objective: prove local scheduler continuation through Forgejo/self-hosted runner semantics across Darwin/Wolfram.
Last verified-good transition: deterministic scheduler/balancer logic can enforce max one lease per host; Darwin is reachable through the already-authorized SSH bootstrap path; durable PR evidence survived reporter blockage.
First missing transition: discover/establish the authoritative private Forgejo Actions endpoint and attach host-specific self-hosted runners so steady-state dispatch no longer depends on SSH shell-driving.
Existing evidence: PR #134; #133 exact lease `43f7c053fdce4d1b8b66ef52dc628704`; reporter artifact_count=1/check_count=3; PR #132 evidence-publisher primitive.
Blocker class: capability / control-plane endpoint discovery.
Semantic work status: partial.
Retry safety: continuation_only. Do not rerun #133.
Minimum missing representation/capability: one authoritative Forgejo URL/repository Actions control plane visible to runner registration, plus `darwin` and `wolfram` runner registration/state evidence. If Forgejo is already alive on Darwin under a local/tailnet route, discover and reuse it rather than create a second instance.
Next safe continuation: bounded Darwin-host successor that verifies the existing Forgejo service/config, enables only the already-intended private Actions path if needed, registers a Darwin runner, then proves one Actions job; add Wolfram runner only after the same endpoint is proven reachable. SSH remains bootstrap/admin only.
requires_pasha: false unless registration requires a genuinely unavailable secret/human login.

BUTTERFLY/v1
symptom: scheduler prototype falls back to SSH aliases when Forgejo endpoint discovery fails, while tests still pass.
integration_context: dual-host orchestration can appear operational even though the desired pull-runner control plane is absent.
cocoon: transport capability and target control-plane capability are not distinct enough in readiness state.
possible_feature: explicit `transport_mode = bootstrap_ssh | forgejo_actions` plus readiness invariant `DUAL_HOST_READY => forgejo_actions endpoint + registered runners + real Actions receipt`.
cheapest_falsification: prove one real Darwin Forgejo Actions job without SSH dispatch; then restart runner and prove no duplicate semantic execution.
decision: adopt_now as acceptance invariant.
